name: pixelforge-image-restoration-
description: Self-trained PyTorch models for single-image super-resolution and low-light enhancement - a full pipeline from data to training, evaluation, TorchScript export, FastAPI backend and an interactive web demo.

paragraphs: PixelForge: an end-to-end image restoration pipeline
Self-trained PyTorch models for single-image super-resolution and low-light enhancement, built end to end from data to training, evaluation and deployment.
features: Real modelling: SRCNN, an SRResNet generator with PixelShuffle + residual blocks, and a low-light U-Net with skip connections, all written from scratch.
Full training loop: data loading, Adam + cosine annealing + AMP mixed precision + optional VGG perceptual loss, PSNR/SSIM evaluation, TorchScript export.

Three shipped weights: SR ×4 (PSNR 27.47), SR ×2 (PSNR 32.35) and low-light (PSNR 18.32) — each beats its classical baseline; classical methods remain as automatic fallback if a weight is ever missing.
Quantitative comparison: classical baselines vs. self-trained models on the same validation set; scripts and per-epoch logs are committed and recomputable.

Engineering: CI runs the tests behind a coverage gate, audits dependencies, and builds the frontend; the Docker image runs as a non-root user; the API enforces per-IP rate limiting and ships documentation.

requirements.text: Self-host the FastAPI backend + Next.js frontend

The FastAPI backend (serve/app.py) and the Next.js frontend (web/) are part of the same codebase and can be self-hosted; web/ posts to serve/app.py, which picks the ML engine for a task/scale when a weight is loaded, otherwise a classical baseline.
